event: Elsie wakes to the bread smell with her notebook still open on her chest.
She reads last night's page over: Tamsin, Tilly, and Cora, black, strong, one sugar.

memory.fact: Elsie keeps a notebook of the birthdays and favourite things of people she loves.

event: She waters the four plants and tells Captain the mint all about the rats.

memory.fact: Elsie's houseplants travel with her in a crate, and every one has a name.

event: She laces the halter, pins the clip, and packs bandages, salve and her notebook.

memory.fact: Elsie wears a cropped cream halter top laced up the front, a short sage-green skirt and tall boots.

event: Downstairs she buys rolls hot from the oven, one for each of them.

changes.note: Four hot rolls, a pip each, one for each of them: 106 → 102 pips

event: The baker asks about the Naming; Elsie tells her Enthraller, and the baker goes quiet.

memory.fact: Elsie cannot lie.

event: The baker wraps the rolls anyway, and tells her to bring the paper back.
Elsie crosses to the north side, past the bridge with the cats, in the early sun.

memory.fact: The Crooked Kettle tea house is on the north side, by the bridge with the cats.

pictured.coverAfter: Outside the morning was already warming, and the last of the mist was lifting

event: The Crooked Kettle is narrow, its kettle sign hung askew over the door.

memory.fact: The Crooked Kettle is a narrow tea house of four tables, its kettle sign hung askew over the door.
The Crooked Kettle is a narrow tea house of four tables, its kettle sign hung askew over the door.

event: Cora is at the door already, ledger under her arm, before the clock reaches eight.

memory.fact: The Crooked Kettle is a narrow tea house of four tables, its kettle sign hung askew over the door.
Cora's glossy black hair is pulled into a severe low bun, never a strand loose.
Cora carries a black leather ledger and writes everything down in a small, exact hand.

event: Elsie gives her a roll; Cora holds it a moment as if unsure what it is for, then eats it.
Tilly comes running with her apron on backwards and her vials clinking at her belt.

memory.fact: Tilly wears a cream blouse with rolled sleeves, a too-big scorched apron and a belt of corked vials.

event: Tamsin comes last, at eight on the dot, Margery over her shoulder and her hair wet.

memory.fact: Tilly wears a cream blouse with rolled sleeves, a too-big scorched apron and a belt of corked vials.
Tamsin's hair is a wild mass of copper curls, barely tied back.
Tamsin has sun-kissed golden skin dusted with freckles, almond-shaped green eyes and a crooked grin.

event: Elsie hands out the rolls; Tamsin eats hers in three bites and licks her thumb.
Inside, a tiny old woman behind the counter looks the four of them up and down.

pictured.coverAfter: The door of the Crooked Kettle opened with a jangle of bells, and they

event: She is the keeper; she brews every pot herself, she says, and she wants her cellar back.
She says the rats have gnawed open three chests of her best black tea.

memory.fact: The rats have gnawed open three chests of the keeper's best black tea.
The rats have gnawed open three chests of the keeper's best black tea.

event: She lifts a hatch behind the counter; the cellar below smells of tea and rats.
Tamsin leans Margery by the counter and takes the keeper's coal shovel instead.

memory.fact: Tamsin fights with a great axe she calls Margery.

event: Tilly says she has a smoke that might drive them out, and it is only half finished.

memory.fact: Tilly makes a good burn salve, a pear-tasting fizz for waking up, and an unfinished smoke.

event: Cora says she will stand at the hatch, and opens her ledger.

memory.fact: A hatch behind the counter opens on a low cellar stacked with tea chests.

event: The keeper hands Elsie a lantern; she goes down first, then Tamsin, then Tilly.
The cellar is low and stacked with tea chests, and the dark at the far end moves.

memory.fact: A hatch behind the counter opens on a low cellar stacked with tea chests.
A hatch behind the counter opens on a low cellar stacked with tea chests.
A hatch behind the counter opens on a low cellar stacked with tea chests.

pictured.coverAfter: The cellar was low, so low that Elsie could have laid her palm flat

event: Dozens of fat brown rats, grown sleek on spilled tea and sugar.

memory.fact: The cellar rats are ordinary brown rats, dozens of them, grown fat on spilled tea and sugar.
The cellar rats are ordinary brown rats, dozens of them, grown fat on spilled tea and sugar.
The cellar rats are ordinary brown rats, dozens of them, grown fat on spilled tea and sugar.

event: Elsie and Tamsin stand pressed shoulder to shoulder between the chests.
Tamsin's ears go red in the lantern light; she says the cellar is very small.
Tilly uncorks her smoke, and green smoke pours out far faster than she meant.
The rats run every way at once, over boots and chests, squealing.
One bites Tamsin's ankle; she grips the shovel, and her breathing changes.
Her eyes start to go flat; she lifts the shovel at the nearest shape, which is Tilly.

memory.fact: In her Frenzy Tamsin blacks out and cannot tell friend from foe until it burns out.

event: Elsie takes Tamsin's wrist in both hands and says her name, close and quiet.

memory.fact: Elsie is fiercely brave when a friend is threatened.

event: Elsie only holds on, with no skill in it, and says her name again.

memory.fact: Elsie has never once used her class to make anyone feel anything.

event: Tamsin's eyes clear before the red can take her; the shovel drops, and she is shaking.
Tilly says she is fine, she is fine, and coughs green.
The rats stream out at the far end, through a broken grate into an old culvert.

memory.fact: The rats come in through a broken grate at the cellar's far end, where it meets an old culvert.
The rats come in through a broken grate at the cellar's far end, where it meets an old culvert.

event: They climb up into the tea house with the smoke rolling after them, eyes streaming.
Cora at the hatch has the ledger open, and writes one line.
Elsie asks what she wrote; Cora reads it out: Skills used, none.

memory.fact: Cora's ledger for the Crooked Kettle cellar reads: skills used, none.
Cora's ledger for the Crooked Kettle cellar reads: skills used, none.

event: Tamsin sits on the step outside; Elsie cleans the bite on her ankle and bandages it.
Tamsin says that is how it starts, and she is sorry; Elsie says she came back.

memory.fact: In her Frenzy Tamsin blacks out and cannot tell friend from foe until it burns out.

event: Tamsin looks at her a long time with her ears red, and says she did, didn't she.

changes.note: Bond: Tamsin 15 → 25 (Elsie held on and kept the Frenzy from taking her)

event: Tilly apologises for the smoke; Elsie wipes the soot off her cheek with her thumb.

memory.fact: Tilly talks fast, faster when nervous, and apologises before anything has gone wrong.

event: Tilly goes very still, pink to the ends of her braids.

changes.note: Bond: Tilly 10 → 15 (Elsie wiped the soot off her cheek)

event: When the smoke clears they go down again, and rats are back by the grate already.

memory.fact: The rats come in through a broken grate at the cellar's far end, where it meets an old culvert.
The rats come in through a broken grate at the cellar's far end, where it meets an old culvert.

event: Elsie says they will all come back through it, and the grate wants mending.

memory.fact: Rats driven out of the cellar come back through the grate within a day unless it is mended.
Rats driven out of the cellar come back through the grate within a day unless it is mended.

event: Tamsin bends the bars straight with her hands while Tilly holds the lantern.
Elsie binds the bars with the keeper's wire the way her mother taught her to set a splint.
Tamsin drives the last rats out with the shovel, and the grate holds.

memory.fact: Elsie's party drove out the Crooked Kettle's rats and wired its broken grate shut.
Elsie's party drove out the Crooked Kettle's rats and wired its broken grate shut.
Elsie's party drove out the Crooked Kettle's rats and wired its broken grate shut.

event: They sweep the gnawed tea into sacks and stack the spoiled chests by the hatch.
The keeper comes down, tests the grate with her boot, and grunts.
Upstairs she signs the notice as done, in a hand like a spider's.

changes.note: Experience: 30 / 100 (judged: first F-rank quest, cellar rats, done)
Tamsin experience 0 → 30 (judged: F-rank cellar rats quest done)
Tilly experience 0 → 30 (judged: F-rank cellar rats quest done)

memory.fact: The guild pays a cellar quest once the keeper signs the notice as done.
The guild pays a cellar quest once the keeper signs the notice as done.

event: She sets out her strong black house tea for the four of them, dark enough to stand a spoon in.

memory.fact: The Crooked Kettle is proud of its strong black house tea, brewed dark enough to stand a spoon in.
The Crooked Kettle is proud of its strong black house tea, brewed dark enough to stand a spoon in.
The Crooked Kettle is proud of its strong black house tea, brewed dark enough to stand a spoon in.

event: Elsie puts one sugar in Cora's cup, stirs it, and slides it across.

memory.fact: Cora drinks her tea black and strong with one sugar.
Cora drinks her tea black and strong with one sugar.
Cora drinks her tea black and strong with one sugar.

event: Cora looks at the cup, then at Elsie, and drinks all of it.

changes.note: Bond: Cora 5 (Elsie sugared her tea as she takes it; Cora drank it all)

event: Tilly says the tea is like being hit, and Tamsin laughs till she has to hold the table.
Elsie says it is the best morning she has had in Lanternmere, and means it.
At the guild hall the clerk takes the signed notice and counts out the pay.
They split it three ways at the desk; Tilly has to sit down to count hers.

changes.note: Her third of the four-lantern rats pay: 13 pips, the odd pip to the others: 102 → 115

event: Elsie offers Cora a share; Cora says a Warden is paid by the guild, and almost smiles.

memory.fact: A guild Warden is paid by the guild.
A guild Warden is paid by the guild.
A guild Warden is paid by the guild.

event: Tamsin says the goat in the Underbloom is still on the board; Tilly goes quiet.
Elsie says they will look at it tomorrow, after lunch, and Tilly breathes again.
Cora says the hall's business with them is done for today, and goes to the charcoal door.
Elsie buys a loaf at a stall, and the three of them share it on the canal wall.

changes.note: One pip for a loaf at a stall, shared on the canal wall: 115 → 114 pips

event: Tilly says her father on Gear Street thinks she is still at the College.
She says he makes clocks, and she writes him letters about lectures she is missing.
Elsie takes her hand and says she can tell him when she is ready, and Elsie will come.
Tilly holds Elsie's hand a long time after, and talks about clocks.

changes.note: Bond: Tilly 15 → 20 (told Elsie about her father, held her hand)

event: Tamsin says her mother runs a barge on the Long Cut, and would like Elsie.
Elsie says she would love to meet her; Tamsin chokes on her bread.

changes.note: Bond: Tamsin 25 → 30 (Elsie wants to meet her mother)

event: They walk Tilly to the end of her street and Tamsin to the docks, and part.
Elsie goes back to the Honeycomb and sleeps an hour in the afternoon heat.
She writes to her mother again, a second letter in one week: I have a party.
In the notebook she writes: Tamsin, ankle, check it; Tilly, her father, clocks.
At closing the baker lets her use the ovens for the cost of the firewood.

changes.note: Two pips to the baker for the oven's firewood: 114 → 112 pips
Elsie ends the chapter with 112 pips: 11 lanterns, 2 pips

event: Elsie bakes honey buns, because she is happy and a little worried about Tamsin's eyes.
Through the bakery window the lamplighters' boats go by and light the canal.
She wraps the buns in paper parcels and writes a name on each.
On Cora's she writes black, strong, one sugar, then crosses it out and writes Cora.
She carries the parcels up to the attic and sets them by the door for the morning.
She hums at the round window until the canal goes quiet.
